tip.title: Organic is about the finishing, not the fibre
tip.body: Cotton and organic cotton shed the same nothing: neither is plastic. The difference is what is done to the cloth afterwards. Conventional cotton is grown with pesticides and finished with formaldehyde resins, chlorine bleaching and heavy metal dyes, and that finish is what sits against your face for eight hours.
look: GOTS, which covers the whole supply chain from field to finished garment and bans those finishes
OEKO-TEX Standard 100 as a second best: it tests the finished fabric, but says nothing about how it was grown
skip: "Made with organic cotton" on its own, which is a marketing phrase and not a certification
"Wrinkle resistant" or "easy care", which usually means a formaldehyde based resin finish

order.title: Where to start
order.body: Two things decide the order: how many hours it spends against your skin, and whether heat and friction are in play.

steps.name: Underwear
steps.why: The thinnest skin you have, twelve hours a day, and washed more often than anything else you own.

steps.name: Workout kit and base layers
steps.why: Heat, sweat and friction at once, which is the combination that moves the most out of a fabric.

steps.name: Sleepwear
steps.why: Eight hours with your face against it, every night.

steps.name: T shirts and socks
steps.why: All day contact and a high wash frequency, so they shed on both counts.

steps.name: Outer layers
steps.why: Least skin contact, so last. Fleece sheds the most of anything in the wash, so use a bag rather than replacing a coat you already own.

tip.title: Here, the formula matters more than the tube
tip.body: Most swaps on this list are about what the packaging puts into the thing it holds. Toothpaste is the exception: it goes in your mouth twice a day and what is in it does the work. A paste with a real active in a plastic tube beats a plastic free paste that does nothing for your teeth. Independent testing of 51 toothpastes in 2025 found lead in about 90 percent of them, and it rides in on mined mineral ingredients rather than on the active itself.
look: A real active: fluoride, or hydroxyapatite at around 10 percent
A published heavy metal result, not just a clean looking label
skip: Clay tooth powders, which tested in the thousands of ppb of lead
Charcoal pastes, which abrade enamel and rebuild nothing

tip.title: A bamboo handle is not a plastic free brush
tip.body: The handle is the part everyone photographs and the bristles are the part that goes in your mouth. Most bamboo brushes use nylon bristles, and plant based nylon is still a polymer. Only animal hair is genuinely plastic free, which is a real trade for anyone who would rather not use boar.
look: Boar bristle if you want no polymer at all
A brand that states the bristle material rather than only the handle
skip: "100% biodegradable" on a brush with nylon bristles, which describes the handle only

tip.title: Check the lid, not just the body
tip.body: A glass or steel kettle can still steam against plastic every boil. The water path is the body, the spout, the filter, the lid and the underside of the lid, and manufacturers describe the shell without mentioning the rest. If the inside of the lid is plastic, boiling water is condensing on it every time.
look: A stated stainless or glass lid interior, spout and filter
An exposed stainless element rather than a plastic housed one
skip: "BPA free" as the whole answer, which says one monomer is absent and nothing about the rest

tip.title: Shoes off does more than the vacuum
tip.body: Soles are polyurethane and rubber and they abrade with every step, and they carry in whatever was on the pavement. Taking them off at the door stops the dust arriving rather than catching it later, which is why it belongs beside a vacuum rather than instead of one. A mat outside to knock off and one inside to catch roughly halves what comes in.
look: A place to put shoes by the door, which is what makes the habit stick
skip: Treating a good vacuum as the whole answer while the dust keeps arriving

tip.title: Sheets and pods are held together with a polymer
tip.body: Laundry sheets are the default plastic free recommendation and they are bound with polyvinyl alcohol, written as PVA or PVOH, a synthetic polymer made from petroleum feedstock. A 2021 paper estimated roughly 17,200 metric tons of it goes into US laundry pods each year and argued much of it survives wastewater treatment. Whether it fully biodegrades is genuinely unresolved. Powder in a cardboard box avoids the question.
look: Powder or a bar, in cardboard
Soap or mineral based rather than a film
skip: Detergent sheets and pods, which are PVA whatever the packaging says
